title: autotune: add sane defaults for batching/caching, quantization profiles, and unit-econ tooling
author: Maya Chen
description: Context: We have a number of customer requests and internal benchmarks showing large TCO variance driven by suboptimal batching, missing prefix/KV cache defaults, and inconsistent quantization profiles. This PR introduces three coordinated changes: 1) sensible default batching and caching policies at the router/runtime level to reduce tail latency while improving throughput for common request distributions; 2) a set of vetted quantization profiles (8-bit and 4-bit presets) and a deterministic selection heuristic for model variants; 3) a small unit-economics toolchain and metrics export to help SRE/product teams measure cost per 1K tokens across routes and model variants so we can automate future autotuning decisions. Summary of changes: - router: new default batching policy implemented with dynamic batch horizon and request-age prioritization; exposes policy knobs in config with safe defaults - runtime: KV/prefix caching enabled by default for chat endpoints with LRU eviction and size-based limits per deployment tier - quant-profiles: added quant_profiles.yaml with model-specific presets and an API to select the closest compatible profile at runtime; includes validation tests - uecon-tooling: adds a small CLI that aggregates token-level cost from traces and exports a per-route CSV and Grafana-friendly metrics via prometheus - tests: end-to-end smoke tests covering routing fallback, cache correctness under TTL, and quant selection. Checklist: - [x] design review (ENG-3214) - [x] perf benchmarks (benchmarks/ canary) - [x] security review for default cache changes - [x] docs + console UI notes - [x] rollout plan with canary flags and gradual enablement Rollout plan: feature flag gating with default off for existing Dedicated customers; staged enablement in hosted API with a 24h canary and automatic rollback on regression signals. Linked tickets: ENG-3214, PM-88. Motivation and impact: expected 12-32% reduction in per-token cost for medium-sequence chat workloads due to improved batching and cache hit rates; quant profiles yield 20-60% GPU memory reduction for compatible models with minor perf tradeoffs. Follow-ups: autotune engine to consume unit-econ metrics and recommend per-customer profiles (separate PR).
